name: Jebusites
summary: The Canaanite people who held Jerusalem — then called Jebus — until David captured their stronghold of Zion and made it his capital. A Jebusite, Araunah, sold David the threshing floor on which Solomon's Temple was built.
name_meaning: From Jebus, the old name of Jerusalem; perhaps 'trodden down' or 'threshing place'.

origin.account: The Jebusite is the third of Canaan's descendants. The Jebusites are always counted among the nations of the land, living 'in the mountains' of the central ridge.

lineage.notes: Jerusalem appears earlier as Salem, the city of Melchizedek. Its king at the conquest, Adonizedek, headed an Amorite alliance, suggesting a mixed Amorite–Jebusite population.

homeland.description: A small, fortified city-state on the narrow south-eastern ridge of Jerusalem (the 'City of David'), above the Gihon spring. It sat on the border between Judah and Benjamin.
homeland.modern_location: The City of David (Silwan) and Old City area of Jerusalem.

places.name: Threshing floor of Araunah (Ornan)
places.note: Site of David's altar and Solomon's Temple.

places.name: Gihon spring
places.note: The city's water source; Solomon was anointed there.

timeline.event: Abdi-Heba, king of Urusalim (Jerusalem), writes to Pharaoh in the Amarna letters asking for troops.
Adonizedek of Jerusalem is defeated, but the city is not held; Judah and Benjamin cannot drive out the Jebusites.
A Levite refuses to lodge in Jebus, 'the city of a stranger'.
The Jebusites taunt David that 'the blind and the lame' could keep him out. Joab goes up the 'gutter' (water shaft), and David takes Zion and makes it the City of David.
To stop a plague, David buys Araunah's threshing floor and builds an altar; Solomon later builds the Temple there.
Remaining Jebusites are made forced labourers.

gods: Canaanite deities (probably including Shalem / Zedek, reflected in the names Salem and Adonizedek)
religion.practices: Little is recorded. Araunah offered David his oxen and threshing tools for sacrifice as a gift, but David insisted on paying.

importance: The Jebusites are remembered for the city they held. Jerusalem stayed in their hands for centuries until David took it, making a neutral capital between Judah and the northern tribes. The Temple site came from a Jebusite by honest purchase, at David's insistence: 'neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing.' Zechariah foresees even Israel's enemies incorporated 'as a Jebusite', just as Araunah's people were.

impact.how: Capturing Jebus gave him his capital, 'the city of David'.
Araunah's threshing floor became the site of the Temple.
Became chief captain by leading the assault.

notable_people.name: Adonizedek
notable_people.role: King of Jerusalem at the conquest

notable_people.name: Araunah (Ornan) the Jebusite
notable_people.role: Sold the Temple site to David

key_verses.text: As for the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.

And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither.

And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth: but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.

fate.summary: After David's conquest the Jebusites seem to have lived on peacefully in Jerusalem, as Araunah did, before being absorbed into Israel. By Ezra's time the name survives only in the traditional list of Canaanite nations.

today.summary: No Jebusite people exist today. Their city is Jerusalem, holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims, and excavations in the City of David have uncovered Bronze Age fortifications from their era.
today.modern_legacy: The Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif, the site of the Jebusite threshing floor, is one of the most contested pieces of land in the world.

archaeology.name: Abdi-Heba letters (EA 285–290)
archaeology.significance: Six letters from Jerusalem's pre-Israelite king.

archaeology.name: Gihon spring fortifications and Warren's Shaft
archaeology.discovered: Charles Warren (1867); Ronny Reich & Eli Shukron (1995–2010)
archaeology.significance: Massive towers guarding the spring, and a water system some link to the 'gutter' of 2 Samuel 5:8.
